statement: Three equal circles of radius 2 cm sit side by side in a row, each touching the next. A rectangle is drawn around them so that its top and bottom touch all three circles and its ends touch the end circles. What is the perimeter of the rectangle?

choices.misconception: I used the radius where I needed the diameter, so I worked with a 6 cm by 2 cm rectangle.
I added only the two long sides of 12 cm and forgot the two short ends.
I used the radius, 2 cm, for the height of the rectangle instead of the diameter.
I worked out the area, 12 x 4, instead of the perimeter.

hints: The rectangle's length is three circle widths and its height is one circle width. A circle's width is its diameter, which is twice the radius.
The diameter is 4 cm, so the rectangle is 12 cm long and 4 cm high.

solutions.reliable: Each circle is 2 x 2 = 4 cm across. Three in a row make the rectangle 3 x 4 = 12 cm long, and its height is one diameter, 4 cm. Perimeter: 2 x (12 + 4) = 32 cm. The transferable idea: when circles touch a line or each other, measure across them using the diameter.

whyOnTest: Circle questions test switching from radius to diameter whenever circles touch each other or a boundary.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
